evaluations.label: A
errors: "Working design presentation not yet on the server; save from email into shared folder" - the Industrial Designer said the working design presentation was already in the shared folder; it was the Project Manager's presentation that was only in email
"age segmentation less useful than lifestyle/attitude targeting" - the alternative discussed was income/spending ability and TV ownership, not lifestyle/attitude
"submit before individual work session" - transcript says questionnaire and summary after the meeting, then lunch, then individual work; no submission deadline stated
strengths: Most complete capture of key numbers: 75%/80%, 50%+ losing remotes, 10% of buttons, 65% zapping, EUR 25 retail, EUR 12.50 production
Clear list of agreed functions (locator, large buttons, hidden extras, battery/cradle, brand-consistent look)
Captures scope decisions (TV only, no teletext) and corporate identity (yellow/black, double R, slogan)
Includes the Marketing Expert's offer to email more age data and the individual workstreams
weaknesses: Next-steps section has no owners named and contains the wrong file-upload claim
Duplicate 'Next Steps' headings make structure slightly confusing
Does not explicitly flag that the target group was left unresolved

evaluations.label: B
errors: "Management decided against including teletext support or voice recognition" - management only decided teletext; voice recognition was dropped by the team on cost grounds

Attributes LCD screens and sliding hatches to the technical (UI) presentation - the LCD idea came from the Marketing Expert's research and the sliding panel came up later in discussion, prompted by the Marketing Expert

"Action Items (none)" - the meeting assigned questionnaire/summary, individual work (components concept, UI concept, trend watching), uploading minutes/slides, and the Marketing Expert offered to email more age data
Unresolved question "Would adding a 'find my remote' beep function fit within budget?" - budget was never raised for this; the team agreed to include a locator
Voice recognition dismissed partly due to "potential complexity for the target user" - not stated; reasons were cost and not being needed in a remote
strengths: Outline section follows the meeting order and covers all three presentations
Captures key numbers including EUR 12.50 production and EUR 25 retail
Mentions corporate identity, TV-only scope and the charging cradle idea
weaknesses: Generic speaker labels (Speaker 2/3/4/5) without roles make attribution hard to follow
Says there are no action items, which is wrong and removes the actionable part
Invents open questions and misattributes who decided what
Target group discussion presented with 'teenagers and families' as if a considered outcome without noting it was left open

evaluations.label: C
errors: "The project lead found that their own presentation was not on the server" - it was the Marketing Expert who pointed out the project lead's file was only in email; minor framing
Action items labelled "owner: Speaker 1" while the body says 'project lead' - inconsistent labeling, not a factual error
strengths: Highly accurate with timestamps that let a reader check claims
Clearly separates decided items (TV only, no teletext, simplicity/fashion, core functions) from open ones (target demographic, voice recognition not favored)
Accurately lists the range of target-age suggestions (15-35, under 65, 20-55) and the income-based alternative
Covers prices, brand slogan and colors, sliding panel idea, cradle and living-room space
weaknesses: Action items section lists only the project lead's tasks; team questionnaire/summary and individual assignments are only in the body
Omits the Marketing Expert's offer to email further age data before the next meeting
Leaves out a few details such as the 65% zapping figure and why infrared was favored

evaluations.label: D
errors: "Target group 15-35 years" presented as a decision - the target group was left open, with the team leaning toward defining it by simplicity/fashion or income rather than age
"Investigate technical feasibility for rechargeable battery" as an action item - the remark was to investigate whether it needs a battery at all; no one was assigned rechargeable feasibility work
strengths: Captures main research findings, design principles, infrared choice and functional decisions
Notes voice recognition rejected on price and the EUR 12.5 production limit
weaknesses: Too terse for someone who missed the meeting; little context or reasoning
Action items unassigned and miss the questionnaire/summary, individual work assignments and uploading minutes/slides
Omits the EUR 25 retail price, slogan, sliding-panel concept detail and the unresolved target-group debate

rationale: C is the most accurate and best separates what was decided from what stayed open, with checkable timestamps, though its action-item list is thin. A is the most complete and very useful but contains a wrong claim about which presentation was missing from the shared folder and names no owners. B covers the meeting in outline but states there were no action items, misattributes the voice-recognition decision to management, and invents a budget question. D is accurate in parts but too terse, presents the 15-35 target group as decided, and has weak, unassigned action items.
